title: City of Industry
name: City of Industry
metaTitle: 1031 Exchange Advisory in City of Industry, CA
metaDescription: City of Industry 1031 exchange advisory for owners of large distribution buildings near the 60/57 interchange and the Puente Hills retail parcels nearby.

sections.html: City of Industry does what its name suggests, with a resident population dwarfed by the daily workforce moving through its distribution centers, and an owner selling here is almost always trading large-format logistics space rather than anything residential-adjacent. The freeway convergence that put the city on the map for distribution tenants in the first place is the same reason a replacement search coming out of it tends to move fast, since comparable big-box logistics land is scarce across the wider San Gabriel Valley. That scarcity puts a premium on getting the identification strategy right the first time, since a seller who misjudges timing here has fewer second chances than in a submarket with steadier turnover.

sections.heading: Big-Box Logistics Clustered at the 60/57 Interchange
sections.html:
Where the State Route 60 and State Route 57 freeways come together, City of Industry hosts some of the largest distribution buildings in the eastern part of the county, many built or expanded for e-commerce and third-party logistics tenants that need direct freeway access more than proximity to any particular population center. Clear-height, trailer parking, and dock-door count matter more to underwriting here than they would in a smaller infill industrial submarket.

Puente Hills Mall sits inside city limits as well, a retail anchor that stands somewhat apart from the surrounding logistics buildings, and an owner trading that kind of retail asset is comparing against a different pool of buyers than the distribution-building sellers nearby.

sections.heading: The Property Types Worth Comparing Coming Out of Industry
sections.html:
An identification list assembled after a City of Industry logistics sale generally draws from:

  • Large-format distribution buildings near the 60/57 interchange
  • Third-party logistics and e-commerce fulfillment space
  • Regional retail centered on Puente Hills-area shopping centers
  • Truck terminal and trailer-parking-heavy industrial parcels
  • DST interests for owners exiting active logistics property management

sections.heading: How Lenders Size Loans on Freeway-Convergence Logistics Product
sections.html:
Lenders like the freeway access here, but they also want confirmation that trailer parking and dock-door ratios match what a modern logistics tenant expects, since a building that was competitive a decade ago can fall behind current tenant standards even without any physical decline. A buyer should get a market read on functional obsolescence before finalizing an offer rather than assuming clear-height and dock count alone tell the full story.

Retail near Puente Hills underwrites on a different basis, with anchor tenant health and co-tenancy clauses driving value more than the freeway access that matters so much for the logistics buildings around it.

sections.heading: Moving Fast in a Market That Trades Quickly
sections.html: Because large logistics buildings near the 60/57 interchange draw institutional as well as private buyers, an owner identifying a replacement here should expect competition for anything well-located and should have financing pre-arranged before the forty-five day window opens rather than after. A qualified intermediary who already tracks City of Industry inventory can flag a matching building faster than a cold search once the relinquished property is under contract.

sections.heading: What a City of Industry Purchase Actually Costs Beyond the Price Tag
sections.html:
A numbers-first budget for a City of Industry logistics building should carry a separate line for dock-door and trailer-parking upgrades if the property does not already meet current tenant expectations, since retrofitting an older building to modern logistics standards is a real capital cost rather than a cosmetic one. Roof condition on large-format tilt-up construction also deserves a hard inspection number before closing, given how much square footage a single roof replacement covers on a building this size.

Lifecycle cost on Puente Hills-area retail runs differently, with common-area maintenance and co-tenancy compliance costs that a buyer moving from industrial property should budget for explicitly rather than assume are minor line items, since retail operating costs behave nothing like the largely fixed costs of a single-tenant logistics building. A buyer moving between the two categories should request three years of common-area maintenance reconciliations before finalizing an offer, rather than relying on a broker's summary of average operating costs for the corridor. Building both budgets side by side before making an offer helps an owner decide whether staying in logistics product or diversifying into retail actually produces the better after-cost return on a given piece of relinquished-property equity.

faqs.q: Why does dock-door count matter so much for a City of Industry logistics purchase?
faqs.a: Modern logistics tenants expect a specific ratio of dock doors and trailer parking to building size, and a building that was competitive a decade ago can now be functionally behind current standards even without physical decline. A buyer should get a market read on that before finalizing an offer.

faqs.q: Is Puente Hills retail underwritten the same way as the logistics buildings around it?
faqs.a: No. Retail near Puente Hills is driven more by anchor tenant health and co-tenancy clauses, while the surrounding distribution buildings are underwritten around freeway access, clear height, and dock-door ratios.

faqs.q: Should I expect competition when identifying a replacement property near the 60/57 interchange?
faqs.a: Often, yes. Large, well-located logistics buildings in this corridor draw institutional as well as private buyers, so having financing arranged before the forty-five day identification window opens puts an investor in a stronger position than starting that process after.

faqs.q: Can 1031 Exchange Los Angeles confirm my City of Industry property qualifies for an exchange?
faqs.a: No. This service coordinates planning, property identification, and communication among an investor's advisors. Whether a specific transaction and property qualify is a determination made by the investor's CPA, tax attorney, and qualified intermediary.
